    How it works and what to watch out for

    Every block, mob, item, UI element and texture style has a version window: when it was added and, if it's gone, when it was removed. “Seen” keeps only versions inside the window. “Not there” removes them, but use it with care: a mob or block missing from one screenshot often just means it isn't in view.

    Resource packs can make a new version look old. From 1.14 on, the built-in “Programmer Art” pack brings back the old textures, so old-looking blocks don't rule out newer versions.

    Some features first appeared behind an experimental toggle (e.g. cherry trees, the crafter, pale oak). Unless you tick “Experimental features may be on”, those count from their full release.

    Pictures come from the Minecraft Wiki (stored with this site when available) and show how things look in the current version. Many blocks and mobs looked different in older versions (especially before the 2019 texture update in 1.14), so match the shape and colours rather than every pixel.

    Data: Mojang's version list, the PrismarineJS minecraft-data project (blocks, items, mobs and biomes, 1.7.2 to 26.1) and the Minecraft Wiki. Clues marked “check” are lower confidence.
